book.title: Prophet Abraham (pbuh): The Friend of Allah (A1)

pages.title: Stone Gods
pages.content:
A very long time ago, a boy was born in Babylon. His parents called him Abraham. Abraham was a good and smart boy. He loved Allah very much. Years later, Allah made Abraham His Messenger.

The people in Abraham’s town did not know Allah. They looked at the stars, the moon and the sun. They said, “These are our gods.” They also had stone gods in a special house. The stone gods looked like people or animals. People asked them for help. Abraham knew this was wrong. The stones could not eat, drink, talk, move or hear. Allah taught Abraham the truth.

Abraham’s father made stone gods. Abraham knew they were only stones. He played with them like toys. He rode on their backs and kicked them.

A person who brings Allah's words.
A thing people wrongly pray to.
A small piece of rock.

exercises.title: Abraham’s Town

pages.title: The Star, the Moon and the Sun
pages.content:
Years passed. Abraham was not a small child now. He wanted to know the one true God, the God of everything.

One night, Abraham saw a bright star. He asked, “Is this my god?” Later, the star went away. Then he saw the moon. The moon went away, too. In the morning, Abraham saw the big sun. He asked, “Is this my god?” But the sun went away, too. Abraham knew that Allah never went away.

Allah showed Abraham the right way and made him His Messenger. Allah told him to show his people the right way.

vocabulary.definition: With a lot of light.

Leave; not be there now.

pages.title: Abraham’s Plan
pages.content:
Abraham told his people about Allah, but they did not listen. He made a plan. He wanted to show them the right way. One day, all the people went to a festival. Abraham went into the house of the stone gods. He broke all of them, but he did not break the biggest one. He put the axe on its neck.

The next day, the people went into the building. They saw the broken stones on the floor. They asked Abraham, “Who broke our gods? Did you do this?” Abraham showed them the big stone. He said, “Look at the axe on its neck. Ask it. Can it speak?” The people were angry and very surprised. They said, “But stones cannot speak!”

vocabulary.definition: A big, happy day for many people.

pages.title: The Fire
pages.content:
The angry people shouted, “Burn Abraham! Burn Abraham!” They made a very big fire. Abraham was in a big fire. He was not afraid, because Allah was with him. Allah said to the fire, “O fire, be cold and safe for Abraham.” The fire was cold and did not hurt Abraham. It was like a beautiful garden.

The fire went out. The people were very surprised, because Abraham was safe. Abraham said again, “Allah is the one true God.” But the people still did not listen to him. They still thought they were right.

pages.title: Abraham and the King
pages.content:
Nimrod was the king of Babylon. He heard about the fire. He called Abraham and asked, “Who is your God?” Abraham said, “My God is Allah. He gives life, and He gives death.” Nimrod said, “I can give life and death, too.”

Abraham said, “Allah makes the sun come up in the east. Can you make it come up in the west?” Nimrod had no answer. He could not do this. Only Allah can do it. The king was very angry.

vocabulary.definition: The man who rules a country.
The end of life.

pages.title: A Long Journey
pages.content:
Only two people believed in Allah with Abraham. They were Sarah and Lot. The other people did not listen. Abraham left Babylon. He wanted to tell other people about Allah.

Abraham went on a long journey. He traveled on camels to Syria and Palestine. It was a long, hot and hard journey. After that, Abraham married Hagar. They had a baby son, Ishmael.

One day, Allah told Abraham to travel with Hagar and Ishmael. They traveled for a long time. Then they came to a quiet valley. There were two small hills there, Safa and Marwah.

vocabulary.definition: Think that something is true.

pages.title: Alone in the Valley
pages.content:
Abraham left Hagar and Ishmael near one of the hills. Hagar knew this was Allah’s plan. She said, “Allah will protect us.” There were no trees, no food and no water in the valley.

Abraham went away. He asked Allah to protect his family. After some days, Hagar and little Ishmael had no food or water. The baby was thirsty. Hagar looked for water. She ran from one hill to the other hill, again and again. But there was no water, and there was no one to help her.

vocabulary.definition: Keep someone safe.
Wanting to drink water.

pages.title: Zamzam Water
pages.content:
Ishmael cried for water. Then, water came out under his feet! Hagar saw it and shouted, “Zamzam!” It means “Stop, stop!” She was very happy. She drank the water. Then she gave water to Ishmael.

This water is very famous today. It is called Zamzam. It is a gift from Allah in the desert. Hagar and Ishmael lived near the water. Many people came there because of the water. They built a city. Its name was Mecca.

vocabulary.definition: A thing you give to someone.
A hot, dry place with sand.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Two Kinds of Past

feedback.correct: Good. You found the two kinds of past.
feedback.incorrect: Say the verb today: shout, come … Does it add -ed or change?

languageFocusExercises.question: Which form tells the past?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The story is in the past: drank, gave. But “today” is now: This water is very famous today.

pages.title: The House of Allah
pages.content:
Abraham visited his family in Mecca many times. One day, Allah told Abraham to build His house, the Ka’ba. Abraham said, “Ishmael, Allah gave me an important job. You will help me.” Ishmael said, “Yes, I will help you.”

Father and son built the Ka’ba together. Today, Muslims of all colors visit the Ka’ba for Hajj. Hajj helps us remember Abraham and his family.

Many years later, Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) was born in Ishmael’s family. He told people Abraham’s message: “There is no god but Allah. He has no partner.”

exercises.title: Born in Babylon

pages.title: Master Glossary
pages.content: Review all key vocabulary from the story in one place.

vocabulary.definition: A person who brings Allah's words.
vocabulary.storyExample: Years later, Allah made Abraham His Messenger.

vocabulary.definition: A thing people wrongly pray to.
vocabulary.storyExample: They said, “These are our gods.”

vocabulary.definition: A small piece of rock.
vocabulary.storyExample: They also had stone gods in a special house.

vocabulary.definition: What is really true.
vocabulary.storyExample: Allah taught Abraham the truth.

vocabulary.definition: Hit with your foot.
vocabulary.storyExample: He rode on their backs and kicked them.

vocabulary.definition: With a lot of light.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: The Star, the Moon and the Sun
vocabulary.storyExample: One night, Abraham saw a bright star.

vocabulary.definition: A small light in the night sky.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: The Star, the Moon and the Sun
vocabulary.storyExample: One night, Abraham saw a bright star.

vocabulary.definition: Leave; not be there now.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: The Star, the Moon and the Sun
vocabulary.storyExample: Later, the star went away.

vocabulary.definition: The big light in the night sky.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: The Star, the Moon and the Sun
vocabulary.storyExample: Then he saw the moon.

vocabulary.definition: The good and true path.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: The Star, the Moon and the Sun
vocabulary.storyExample: Allah showed Abraham the right way and made him His Messenger.

vocabulary.definition: A big, happy day for many people.
vocabulary.storyExample: One day, all the people went to a festival.

vocabulary.definition: Make something go into pieces.
vocabulary.storyExample: He broke all of them, but he did not break the biggest one.

vocabulary.definition: A tool for cutting trees.
vocabulary.storyExample: He put the axe on its neck.

vocabulary.definition: Very unhappy because of something bad.
vocabulary.storyExample: The people were angry and very surprised.

vocabulary.definition: Feeling "Oh! I did not know that!".
vocabulary.storyExample: The people were angry and very surprised.

vocabulary.definition: Something very hot, red and yellow.
vocabulary.storyExample: They made a very big fire.

vocabulary.definition: Feeling that something bad will happen.
vocabulary.storyExample: He was not afraid, because Allah was with him.

vocabulary.definition: Make a person feel pain.
vocabulary.storyExample: The fire was cold and did not hurt Abraham.

vocabulary.definition: Not in danger; nothing bad happens.
vocabulary.storyExample: The people were very surprised, because Abraham was safe.

vocabulary.definition: Say something very loudly.
vocabulary.storyExample: The angry people shouted, “Burn Abraham! Burn Abraham!”

vocabulary.definition: The man who rules a country.
vocabulary.storyExample: Nimrod was the king of Babylon.

vocabulary.definition: The end of life.
vocabulary.storyExample: Abraham said, “My God is Allah. He gives life, and He gives death.”

vocabulary.definition: Think that something is true.
vocabulary.storyExample: Only two people believed in Allah with Abraham.

vocabulary.definition: A long trip from one place to another.
vocabulary.storyExample: Abraham went on a long journey.

vocabulary.definition: A big desert animal with a hump.
vocabulary.storyExample: He traveled on camels to Syria and Palestine.

vocabulary.definition: Low land between hills or mountains.
vocabulary.storyExample: Then they came to a quiet valley.

vocabulary.definition: A small mountain.
vocabulary.storyExample: There were two small hills there, Safa and Marwah.

vocabulary.definition: Keep someone safe.
vocabulary.storyExample: She said, “Allah will protect us.”

vocabulary.definition: Wanting to drink water.
vocabulary.storyExample: The baby was thirsty.

vocabulary.definition: A thing you give to someone.
vocabulary.storyExample: It is a gift from Allah in the desert.

vocabulary.definition: A hot, dry place with sand.
vocabulary.storyExample: It is a gift from Allah in the desert.

vocabulary.definition: Make a house or a building.
vocabulary.storyExample: One day, Allah told Abraham to build His house, the Ka’ba.

vocabulary.definition: A visit to Mecca for worship.
vocabulary.storyExample: Today, Muslims of all colors visit the Ka’ba for Hajj.

vocabulary.definition: A person who is with you in something.
vocabulary.storyExample: He told people Abraham’s message: “There is no god but Allah. He has no partner.”

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review the language from all chapters.

exercises.title: Look: Two Kinds of Past
exercises.instructions: Put each verb in the right group.
exercises.question: How does each verb show the past?
exercises.explanation: Many verbs add -ed: ask → asked, shout → shouted. Some verbs change: see → saw, break → broke, come → came, build → built.

feedback.correct: Well done. You found the two kinds of past.
feedback.incorrect: Say the verb today: ask, see … Does it add -ed or change?

exercises.title: Practise: Was or Were
exercises.question: One or many?
exercises.explanation: One person: was. Two or more: were.

feedback.incorrect: Abraham = one. The people = many.

exercises.title: Practise: Can or Could Not
exercises.question: Is it possible?

formChoices.sentence: Nimrod [choice] make the sun come up in the west.

exercises.explanation: Can / cannot: now. Could / could not: in the past.

feedback.incorrect: Can a stone speak? Could Nimrod do it?

exercises.title: Practise: Will
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
exercises.question: What will happen?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Hagar said, “Allah [blank] protect us.” Abraham said, “You will [blank] me.” Ishmael said, “Yes, I [blank] help you.”
exercises.explanation: Will + verb: will protect, will help.

feedback.incorrect: Find the will sentences in Chapters 7 and 9.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Word
exercises.instructions: Find the wrong word. Write the right word.
exercises.question: Which word is wrong?
exercises.explanation: “Break” and “see” change in the past: broke, saw.

feedback.incorrect: Break → broke. See → saw. They do not take -ed.

exercises.title: Use: My Week
exercises.instructions: Write three sentences about your week.
exercises.question: What did you do this week?
exercises.explanation: Use one past verb, one can and one will.

discussionPrompts.question: One past verb: “I visited …”
discussionPrompts.example: I visited my friend.

discussionPrompts.question: One “can”: “I can …”
discussionPrompts.example: I can swim.

discussionPrompts.question: One “will”: “I will …”
discussionPrompts.example: I will read a book tomorrow.

exercises.title: The Story of Abraham
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: The fire did not hurt Abraham.
Abraham and Ishmael built the Ka’ba.

exercises.explanation: Stone gods (Chapter 3) → the fire (Chapter 4) → leaving Babylon (Chapter 6) → the Ka’ba (Chapter 9).

feedback.correct: Great! You know the story of Abraham.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the order of the chapters.
